name: Four-layer wave-sequenced cinematic pad: crossfaded seconds-based wave sequence, released keys layer, LFO-rate-modulated analog layer, tempo-locked rhythmic step layer with shape/ratchet/probability
goal: Build an evolving cinematic pad from four complementary layers: (1) a smooth wave sequence that crossfades between several string-like sources at seconds-based step times (~1 s) with slow attack/release, compression, tape delay and reverb; (2) a plain keys/piano layer with long release, gentle velocity-sensitive filter envelope and its own delay; (3) a synthetic layer sequencing between two different saw sources through a filter envelope, with a free-running LFO whose rate is itself modulated by a second slow free-running LFO (plus a touch of pitch deviation and panning from that LFO); (4) a tempo-locked (quarter-note) step layer with crossfade off, using saw-down/triangle step shapes on cutoff, double/triple ratchets at reduced probability and a tempo-synced filter LFO — then balance layers and put the busiest one on a macro.
prerequisites: Synth with ≥4 layers/voices per patch, a wave-sequence or step-sequence of oscillator sources (Web Audio: per-step source crossfade via GainNodes scheduled on AudioParam timelines, implementation note)
Filter + envelopes per layer, 2+ LFOs with free-run mode and LFO→LFO-rate routing

inputs.name: tempo
inputs.description: Project tempo for the rhythmic layer

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Use original/free samples or generic waves in place of factory multisamples — no factory sample/preset names copied.
Presenter improvised from an init patch; values are approximate and by ear.
All four layers together can get busy — balance levels and use a macro on the rhythmic/analog layer.

steps.action: Layer 1 (smooth wave sequence): choose 3–4 string-like sources moving from acoustic chamber/orchestral strings toward a synthetic string; set step time in seconds (~1 s per step) with crossfade on so each source melts into the next.
Layer 1 envelope + FX: slower attack, some release, lengthen crossfade slightly; add compression, tape delay and master reverb (chorus not needed).

Layer 2 (keys): a single piano/keys source with a long, nice release; optionally lower cutoff with a release-shaped filter envelope, make it velocity-sensitive, add a different delay. A phaser was tried but softened the attack — compression worked better to give the keys impact over the strings.
steps.expect: Articulate keys line cutting through the pad

steps.action: Layer 3 (analog-style): wave-sequence between two different saw sources for variety; filter with filter envelope and tape delay.
steps.expect: Synthetic brass/string tone with subtle source changes

steps.action: Layer 3 motion: route a free-running LFO to the layer (e.g. filter/level), then use a second, very slow free-running LFO (the spare pan LFO) to modulate the first LFO's speed so it speeds up and slows down; use that slow LFO also for a tiny pitch deviation and for panning.
steps.expect: Breathing modulation whose speed drifts over time

steps.action: Layer 4 (rhythmic): new wave sequence in tempo mode (quarter notes, speed up later) through synthetic/spectral and vocal-like sources; turn crossfade off so steps are audible.

Shape the steps: give the step lane a saw-down shape (a pulse of 100 that decays to 0 = pseudo-envelope per step), lower cutoff and apply the step shape to cutoff; add double/triple ratchets on some steps and lower their probability so it isn't jarring; add a tempo-synced filter LFO and interesting delays.
steps.expect: Plucky, sometimes-ratcheted pulses inside the pad

steps.action: Key-sync the rhythmic layer's steps so chords start in sync; optionally jump the last step up one or two octaves.
steps.expect: Rhythmic layer locks to each chord start

steps.action: Balance: bring the busy analog layer down, map it (or the rhythmic layer) to a macro knob for real-time control.
steps.expect: Layers sit together; density controllable live

verification: Layer 1 alone changes timbre smoothly with no audible steps; layer 4 alone changes audibly on the beat.
Layer 3's modulation rate is audibly not constant over ~10 s.
Ratchets don't fire on every bar when probability is reduced.
